bull.t: Rapid revenue growth and high gross margin
bull.b: Rapid revenue growth and approximately 90% gross margin indicate improving product economics as VIZZ commercialization develops. If sales continue scaling, the high gross-margin profile could allow incremental revenue to contribute meaningfully toward operating costs and support durable earnings potential.

Repeat purchasing provides evidence that patients may continue using VIZZ after initial adoption, strengthening the commercial model beyond one-time prescriptions. Mature cohorts approaching five annual packs could support recurring revenue and improve customer economics as the company expands acquisition channels.

International partnerships and multiple regulatory reviews broaden potential access to VIZZ without requiring LENZ to build every overseas commercial operation itself. Approval and launch progress across these markets could diversify revenue sources and extend the product's addressable opportunity over time.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and external funding dependence
bear.b: The substantial cash deficit shows that current operations do not fund the company's development and commercialization requirements. Continued burn can reduce financial flexibility and increase reliance on external capital, particularly if revenue growth does not catch up with spending over the next several quarters.

Deep and widening operating losses indicate that the commercial launch has not yet reached the scale needed to absorb the cost structure. Until revenue grows substantially or expenses are reduced, negative operating leverage will remain a major constraint on profitability and capital efficiency.

Limited retail traction restricts the breadth of distribution and makes it harder to establish refill and persistence behavior across the full market. Weak conversion from awareness into recurring prescribing could slow durable patient growth and leave commercialization overly dependent on e-pharmacy performance.
